mainTopic: Which camps a מצורע, זב and בעל קרי must leave: testing a קל וחומר, רבי יהודה vs. רבי שמעון, and support for רבי יוחנן
overview: The גמרא first finishes an earlier answer: a זב can also become impure באונס, as רב הונא teaches about his first sighting. It then tests a קל וחומר about which camps a מצורע must leave. Each attempt is met with 'אדרבה'. A זב has his own strictnesses. The extra word in 'וכל זב' brings in a בעל קרי, but he seems stricter too, since he becomes impure from any amount. Following רבי נתן, a בעל קרי needs a minimum amount, so the קל וחומר stands. The גמרא explains that 'וכל צרוע' is written only to match 'וכל זב'. It also explains that רבי יהודה does not learn the three camps from the פסוק like רבי שמעון, because he needs it for רבי אליעזר's rule about פסח הבא בטומאה. Finally, the דרשה that 'וכל זב' includes a בעל קרי supports רבי יוחנן, who says a בעל קרי is sent outside two camps. A teaching comparing a בעל קרי to מגע שרץ is explained as being about impurity באונס, not camps, and a new objection begins at the end of the amud.

steps.title: A זב also becomes impure through an accident
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers an earlier objection: the objection treated becoming impure באונס as a special stringency, but a זב shares it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a case like this, a זב also becomes impure through an accident, like the view of רב הונא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering an objection raised on the previous amud. It says the stringency mentioned there, becoming impure even through an accident, is true of a זב as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An argument was blocked because one side seemed to have a special strictness: impurity even באונס. The גמרא answers that this is not unique, since a זב can also become impure באונס. So that difference cannot block the comparison. The proof for this comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case like this; in this respect
A man with an abnormal discharge that makes him ritually impure
Through an accident or outside cause
He does become impure (the doubled verb adds emphasis)

phrases.english: In a case like this —
phrases.notes: In this respect, comparing the two cases this way

phrases.english: a zav also becomes impure through an accident
in accordance with Rav Huna.
phrases.notes: The source is quoted in the next step

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא — זָב נָמֵי טַמּוֹיֵי מְטַמֵּי בְּאוֹנֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers an objection raised on the previous amud
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the claimed unique stringency is shared by both sides
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Impurity באונס is a strictness that only one side has
steps.terutzMaskana: A זב also becomes impure באונס, so this difference does not break the comparison

steps.title: רב הונא: a זב's first sighting makes him impure even by accident
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רב הונא to support the claim that a זב can become impure באונס.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב הונא said: The first sighting of a זב makes him impure even through an accident.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the previous step: רב הונא's rule about a זב's first discharge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the severe seven-day impurity of a זב needs at least two discharges, and we check whether an outside cause produced them. רב הונא teaches that the very first sighting makes him impure even if it came from an accident. This proves that a זב also has impurity באונס.

keyTerms.meaning: The first sighting, meaning the first discharge
An אמורא (a sage of the גמרא) whose rule is quoted here
Makes impure

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא is talking only about the FIRST sighting. He is not saying that every later discharge of a זב counts even if it was caused by an accident.

phrases.english: For Rav Huna said:
The first sighting of a zav
makes impure even through an accident.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the answer in step 1
steps.raayaObject: That a זב becomes impure באונס
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא: ראיה ראשונה של זב מטמאה באונס

steps.title: In what way is a מצורע stricter than a זב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the specific ways a מצורע is stricter than a זב. This sets up a possible קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the stringency of a מצורע over a זב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. To argue that a מצורע must be sent out further than a זב, it first needs to show what makes a מצורע stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if one case is clearly stricter. The idea is this: if a זב is sent out of certain camps, a stricter מצורע should be sent out even further. So the גמרא first asks what that extra strictness is.

keyTerms.meaning: Its stringency or strictness
A person with צרעת, a skin affliction that brings impurity
An argument from a lighter case to a stricter case (a fortiori)

phrases.english: What is the stringency of a leper over a zav?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new attempt: a קל וחומר from זב to מצורע
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What makes a מצורע stricter than a זב

steps.title: The מצורע grows his hair, tears his clothes, and may not have relations
steps.stepSummary: A מצורע has unique strict rules: פריעה, פרימה, and a ban on תשמיש המטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he must let his hair grow wild and tear his clothes, and he is forbidden in marital relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question by listing three rules that apply only to a מצורע and not to a זב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These three rules show that a מצורע lives under special mourning-like restrictions. Since a זב has none of these, a מצורע seems stricter, and that would support the קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: Letting the hair grow wild
Tearing the clothes
Marital relations
Because; since

phrases.english: For he requires letting his hair grow and tearing his garments,
and he is forbidden in marital relations.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פריעה, פרימה, and the ban on תשמיש המטה

steps.title: On the contrary, a זב is stricter
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר is blocked: a זב has strict impurity rules that a מצורע lacks, namely משכב ומושב and היסט.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, a זב is stricter, since he makes impure what he lies or sits on, and he makes an earthenware vessel impure by moving it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back, saying 'אדרבה': you could just as easily say the זב is stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב makes a bed or seat impure just by lying or sitting on it, without touching it directly. He also makes a כלי חרס impure by moving it, even though a כלי חרס normally becomes impure only from its inside. Since each side has its own strictness, neither one is clearly stricter, and the קל וחומר falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
What one lies on and what one sits on
An earthenware vessel
Moving something, even without touching it

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic rule of קל וחומר: if each side has its own separate strictness, you cannot call either one 'stricter', and the argument fails.

phrases.english: On the contrary, a zav is more severe,
for he imparts impurity to what he lies on and sits on,
and he imparts impurity to an earthenware vessel by moving it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim of step 4 that a מצורע is stricter
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר from זב to מצורע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The זב has his own strictness (משכב ומושב and היסט), so the מצורע is not clearly stricter

steps.title: The פסוק 'וכל זב' includes a בעל קרי, who is lighter than a מצורע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the comparison: the extra word 'וכל' includes a בעל קרי, and a מצורע is clearly stricter than a בעל קרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'זב' and 'וכל זב' to include a בעל קרי. And a מצורע is stricter than a בעל קרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by picking a different, lighter case. Since the פסוק includes a בעל קרי in the camp rule, the קל וחומר can run from the בעל קרי to the מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וכל' (and every) widens the rule beyond a זב to a בעל קרי, whose impurity is similar. A בעל קרי lacks the special strictnesses of a זב, so the 'אדרבה' from step 5 no longer applies. The new argument is: if a בעל קרי is sent out of the camp, then surely a מצורע is too.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק says
'And every', a word that widens the rule to include more cases
To include
A man who had a seminal emission

phrases.english: The verse states not just 'zav' but 'and any zav,'
to include one who had a seminal emission.
And a leper is more severe than one who had a seminal emission.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא ״זָב״, ״וְכׇל זָב״, לְרַבּוֹת בַּעַל קֶרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'אדרבה' of step 5 by switching to a lighter comparison case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the starting point of the קל וחומר to a lighter case found through a ריבוי (an extra word in the פסוק)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר must start from a זב, who has his own strictnesses
steps.terutzMaskana: Start from a בעל קרי, who is included by 'וכל זב' and is lighter than a מצורע

steps.title: How is a מצורע stricter than a בעל קרי? As we said
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes a מצורע stricter than a בעל קרי and points back to the same three rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is his stringency? As we said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the new claim. It answers that the מצורע's strictness is the same as before: פריעה, פרימה, and the ban on relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new strictness is offered. The גמרא simply reuses the list from step 4. This sets up a new test of whether a בעל קרי has a strictness of his own.

keyTerms.meaning: As we said (pointing back to an earlier statement)

phrases.english: And what is his stringency?
As we said.
phrases.notes: Hair growing, tearing garments, ban on marital relations

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks the claim at the end of step 6
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What makes a מצורע stricter than a בעל קרי
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The same three rules listed in step 4

steps.title: On the contrary, a בעל קרי is stricter, since any amount makes him impure
steps.stepSummary: The new קל וחומר is also blocked: a בעל קרי becomes impure from even the tiniest amount, while נגעים have a minimum size.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, a בעל קרי is stricter, since he becomes impure with any amount!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back again with 'אדרבה', showing that a בעל קרי also has a strictness the מצורע does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה gives no minimum amount for קרי, so even a tiny bit makes a person impure. A נגע of צרעת, however, must be a certain size. So the בעל קרי has his own strictness, and the second attempt at a קל וחומר is weakened just like the first.

keyTerms.meaning: With any amount, even the smallest
Stricter; more severe

steps.whatToRemember: Both attempts to prove by קל וחומר that a מצורע is sent further than others (first from a זב, then from a בעל קרי) are met with 'אדרבה', because each case seems to have a strictness of its own. The next step rescues the second attempt by following רבי נתן.

phrases.english: On the contrary: one who had a seminal emission is more severe,
for he becomes impure with any amount!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim of steps 6 and 7 that a מצורע is stricter than a בעל קרי
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר from בעל קרי to מצורע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A בעל קרי becomes impure במשהו, while נגעים need a minimum size, so the מצורע is not clearly stricter

steps.title: Following רבי נתן, a בעל קרי also needs a minimum amount
steps.stepSummary: The view follows רבי נתן, who says a זב needs a minimum amount of discharge. A בעל קרי is linked to a זב, so he also needs a minimum. The challenge from Step 8 disappears.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי נתן. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי נתן says in the name of רבי ישמעאל that a זב becomes impure only from a discharge big enough to block the opening of the organ, but the חכמים disagreed with him. And a בעל קרי is linked by a היקש to a זב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 8. It says that, according to רבי נתן, a בעל קרי does not become impure from the tiniest amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said a בעל קרי is stricter because he becomes impure from any amount, while נגעים need a minimum size. רבי נתן says a זב needs a minimum amount, and the Torah links a בעל קרי to a זב, so a בעל קרי needs a minimum too. Now the בעל קרי has no extra strictness, so the קל וחומר from the בעל קרי to the מצורע works again.

keyTerms.meaning: Enough discharge to block the opening of the organ. This is רבי נתן's minimum amount.
The חכמים did not agree with him.
Was linked by a היקש, a Torah comparison that applies the rules of one case to another.
A minimum required amount or size.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is ruling like רבי נתן in practice. The חכמים disagree with him. The גמרא only shows that this view of the camps can rely on רבי נתן.

phrases.english: He holds in accordance with Rabbi Natan.
As it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says in the name of Rabbi Yishmael:
A zav needs a discharge enough to block the tip of the organ,
phrases.notes: So a זב becomes impure only from a minimum amount.

phrases.english: But the Sages did not agree with him.
And one who had a seminal emission is compared to a zav.
phrases.notes: So the same minimum applies to a בעל קרי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 8 by removing the stringency it claimed a בעל קרי has.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the view to a specific תנא (רבי נתן) whose opinion removes the problem
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A בעל קרי becomes impure from any amount, so he is stricter than a מצורע in one way and the קל וחומר fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי נתן, a בעל קרי, like a זב, needs a minimum amount. The מצורע has no weaker point, and the קל וחומר stands.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק say 'and any leper'?
steps.stepSummary: The word 'כל' added to זב includes a בעל קרי. So what does the 'כל' added to צרוע include?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need the word 'וכל' in 'and any צרוע'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a side question about the wording of the פסוק. The word 'כל' teaches something for זב, so what does it teach for צרוע?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this approach, extra words like 'כל' are read as adding cases. The 'כל' by זב was already used to include a בעל קרי, as Step 6 explained. The 'כל' by צרוע seems to add nothing, so the גמרא asks why it is there.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? This asks what an extra word or phrase teaches.
A person with צרעת, a leper. Same as מצורע.

phrases.english: Why do I need "and any leper"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the main argument is saved, the גמרא checks a leftover word in the same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word 'כל' in 'כל צרוע' comes to include.

steps.title: The word is there to match the phrase 'any זב'
steps.stepSummary: 'כל צרוע' does not teach a new law. It is written so that the wording matches 'כל זב'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the פסוק wrote 'any זב', it also wrote 'any צרוע'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'כל' by צרוע is only there to keep the style of the פסוק consistent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every extra word must teach a law. Here the 'כל' by צרוע simply follows the pattern of 'כל זב', which does teach something. So no new case is added for צרוע.

keyTerms.meaning: Since; because of. It introduces a reason based on matching wording.
Also.

steps.whatToRemember: 'אַיְּידֵי דִּכְתִיב' means a word is written only to match a nearby phrase, not to teach a new law.

phrases.english: Since it is written "any zav,"
it is also written "any leper."

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'כל' by צרוע is written only to match 'כל זב'. It adds no new law.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי יהודה use the פסוק like רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון learns the three camps straight from the פסוק. That seems right, so why does רבי יהודה reject it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה: doesn't רבי שמעון say it well?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה. רבי שמעון's reading of the פסוק looks good, so why doesn't רבי יהודה accept it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון reads 'כל צרוע, וכל זב, וכל טמא לנפש' as listing three groups, each sent out of a different camp. רבי יהודה instead built his rule on a קל וחומר and on extra words. The question is phrased as a question, but it is really an attack: what will רבי יהודה do with this פסוק?

keyTerms.meaning: He says it well. This is a challenge that the other opinion seems correct.
The three camps: of the שכינה, of the לויה, and of ישראל.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda:
doesn't Rabbi Shimon speak well?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, שַׁפִּיר קָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the larger argument between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון about how to learn the camps.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's choice not to learn the three camps from the פסוק itself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק clearly lists three groups, and רבי שמעון's reading is simple and good. רבי יהודה must explain what the פסוק teaches if not the three camps.

steps.title: רבי יהודה needs the פסוק for the case of פסח הבא בטומאה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה uses the פסוק for רבי אליעזר's teaching. When those impure from a dead body are not sent out, such as at a פסח הבא בטומאה, זבין and מצורעין who enter the עזרה are not liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs that פסוק for what a ברייתא teaches. רבי אליעזר says: I might have thought that if זבין and מצורעין pushed their way into the עזרה during a פסח that is brought in impurity, they would be liable. So the פסוק says, 'They shall send out of the camp any צרוע and any זב and anyone impure from a dead body.' This teaches that when those impure from a dead body are sent out, זבין and מצורעין are sent out. When those impure from a dead body are not sent out, זבין and מצורעין are not sent out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יהודה. The פסוק is already being used for a different law, so he cannot use it to learn the three camps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר learns that the three groups in the פסוק are tied together. When most of the people are impure from a dead body, the פסח is brought in impurity and those impure from a dead body are not sent out. Then זבין and מצורעין who force their way in are not liable either, even though it is still forbidden. Since the פסוק teaches this link, רבי יהודה cannot also use it to teach separate camps.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it for something else. The פסוק is already used for another teaching.
A קרבן פסח brought while most of the people are impure from a dead body.
The courtyard of the בית המקדש.
People who are impure from contact with a dead body.
Are sent out of the camp.
Therefore the פסוק says. It introduces the source that teaches the law.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה does not learn the three camps from 'וישלחו מן המחנה' because he uses that פסוק for רבי אליעזר's rule. The three groups are linked, so when טמאי מתים are not sent out, זבין and מצורעין are not liable for entering.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Not sent out' here does not mean זבין and מצורעין may enter the עזרה. It means they are not liable for punishment. Entering is still forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how one פסוק can only carry one main teaching in a מחלוקת. It also gives a practical rule for a פסח הבא בטומאה.

phrases.english: He needs that verse for what was taught in a baraita,
Rabbi Eliezer says:
One might think that if zavin and lepers pushed
and entered the Temple courtyard
during a Paschal offering brought in impurity,
perhaps they would be liable,
therefore the verse states:
"That they send out from the camp
any leper and any zav
and anyone impure by reason of a corpse."
At a time when those impure from a corpse are sent out,
zavin and lepers are sent out;
when those impure from a corpse are not sent out,
zavin and lepers are not sent out.
phrases.notes: Meaning they are not liable for entering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 12 by showing the פסוק is used for another teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The פסוק is needed for a different teaching (מיבעי ליה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק has nothing else to teach, so רבי יהודה should learn the three camps from it.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה uses the פסוק for רבי אליעזר's rule linking זבין and מצורעין to טמאי מתים, so it cannot also teach the three camps.

steps.title: The extra word 'and every' supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The דרשה that 'וכל זב' includes a בעל קרי supports רבי יוחנן, who says a בעל קרי is sent outside two camps.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: The verse says 'and every זב' instead of just 'זב' in order to include a בעל קרי. This supports רבי יוחנן, because רבי יוחנן said: The tunnels under the Temple were not made holy, and a בעל קרי is sent outside two camps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the earlier ברייתא that 'וכל זב' includes a בעל קרי. It says this teaching backs up a ruling of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב must leave two camps: מחנה שכינה (the Temple) and מחנה לויה (the Temple Mount). If the פסוק about the זב also includes a בעל קרי, then a בעל קרי must also leave both camps. That is exactly what רבי יוחנן rules.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said', used to quote an earlier teaching and discuss it
To include, meaning an extra word adds another case
It supports him
Tunnels under the Temple area
Is sent out
Two camps, here מחנה שכינה and מחנה לויה

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole section. Is a בעל קרי treated like a זב (two camps) or like a lighter טמא (one camp)?

phrases.english: The Master said:
'A zav', 'and every zav' —
phrases.notes: The extra word 'every' is being explained.

phrases.english: to include a person who had a seminal emission.
This supports Rabbi Yochanan.
For Rabbi Yochanan said:
The tunnels were not sanctified,
phrases.notes: The tunnels under the Temple did not have the Temple's holiness.

phrases.english: and a person who had a seminal emission is sent out
outside the two camps.
phrases.notes: מחנה שכינה and מחנה לויה, just like a זב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the 'וכל זב' דרשה from Step 6 and uses it to support רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a בעל קרי is sent outside two camps.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that reads 'וכל זב' as including a בעל קרי.

steps.title: A teaching compares a בעל קרי to touching a שרץ
steps.stepSummary: A teaching says a בעל קרי is like one who touched a שרץ. Perhaps that means he is sent out of only one camp.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: A בעל קרי is like one who touched a שרץ. Doesn't this mean they are alike regarding their camps?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן with a teaching that compares a בעל קרי to someone who touched a שרץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who touched a שרץ is sent out of only מחנה שכינה. He may stay in מחנה לויה. If a בעל קרי is 'like' him regarding camps, then a בעל קרי also leaves only one camp, which contradicts רבי יוחנן's 'two camps'.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection from a תנאי source
Contact with a dead creeping creature, which causes a light טומאה
Isn't it that…? A suggested reading used to build a challenge
Their camps, meaning which areas they must leave

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A person who had a seminal emission is like one who touched a creeping creature.
Is it not regarding their camps?
phrases.notes: If so, he would leave only מחנה שכינה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling supported in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a בעל קרי is sent outside two camps.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A comparison to מגע שרץ suggests one camp, not two.

steps.title: The comparison is about the kind of impurity
steps.stepSummary: The comparison is about their טומאה, not their camps.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is regarding their impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the teaching compares the two people's טומאה, not which camps they must leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are only impure until evening, a light level of טומאה. So the comparison says nothing about camps, and רבי יוחנן is safe.

keyTerms.meaning: Their impurity, meaning the type and length of the טומאה

phrases.english: No, it is regarding their impurity.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the scope of the comparison
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison is about the level of טומאה.

steps.title: The Torah already says both are impure until evening
steps.stepSummary: A comparison about טומאה would be pointless, since the Torah already writes 'impure until evening' for both. So it must be about camps.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding their impurity?! 'Impure until evening' is written about this one, and 'impure until evening' is written about that one! Rather, isn't it regarding their camps?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the answer. There is no need to compare their impurity, because the Torah states it openly for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah writes 'טמא עד הערב' both for touching a שרץ (ויקרא יא) and for a בעל קרי (ויקרא טו). A teaching would not bother repeating something the פסוקים already say clearly. So the comparison must teach something new, and the challenge says that new thing is the camps.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity that lasts until evening, after טבילה
It is written about him in the Torah
Rather, isn't it…? Pushing back to the first reading

phrases.english: Regarding their impurity?!
For this one, impurity until evening is written,
and for that one, impurity until evening is written!
Rather, is it not regarding their camps!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְטוּמְאָתָם?! הַאי טוּמְאַת עֶרֶב כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of Step 16 and goes back to the challenge of Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the comparison is about טומאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both cases already have 'impure until evening' written in the Torah. The comparison would teach nothing new.

steps.title: A בעל קרי is impure even by accident, like touching a שרץ
steps.stepSummary: The comparison is about טומאה after all. It teaches that a בעל קרי becomes impure even through אונס, just like touching a שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, really it is regarding their impurity. It teaches us that a בעל קרי is like one who touched a שרץ: just as touching a שרץ makes a person impure even by accident, so too a בעל קרי becomes impure even by accident.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps its answer that the comparison is about טומאה. It explains that the comparison teaches a new detail that is not written openly in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is אונס. Touching a שרץ makes a person impure even when it happens by accident. A בעל קרי is the same. This is different from a זב: once he has had his first sighting, a discharge brought on by an outside cause does not count toward his זב status. Since the comparison teaches something new about טומאה, it says nothing about camps, and רבי יוחנן's two-camp ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually. Used to keep the original answer
This is what it teaches us
Makes impure, or becomes impure
By accident, through circumstances beyond one's control

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with a זב. Earlier the גמרא linked a בעל קרי to a זב for the camps. Here, for אונס, a בעל קרי is treated differently from a זב. A later discharge of a זב that came by אונס does not count toward the severe זב status (only his first sighting counts even באונס, as רב הונא said in Step 2). A בעל קרי, however, is always impure even באונס.
steps.whatToRemember: A בעל קרי is like a זב for camps: he is sent out of two camps (רבי יוחנן). He is like מגע שרץ for impurity: impure until evening, even if it happened by accident.

phrases.english: No, actually it is regarding their impurity,
and this is what it teaches us:
that a person who had a seminal emission is like one who touched a creeping creature:
just as touching a creeping creature makes one impure even by accident —
so too a person who had a seminal emission becomes impure even by accident.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְעוֹלָם לְטוּמְאָתָם, וְהָא קָמַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17 by showing a new lesson about טומאה that is not written openly in the Torah.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a new detail that the comparison teaches
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A comparison about טומאה would only repeat 'impure until evening,' so it must be about camps.
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison teaches that a בעל קרי is impure even by אונס. רבי יוחנן's two-camp ruling stands.

steps.title: The גמרא introduces a new objection
steps.stepSummary: With the word 'מֵיתִיבִי', the גמרא announces that it is about to quote an earlier source that seems to contradict the position it has just been defending.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is telling us that a challenge is coming, and the actual source will be quoted in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מֵיתִיבִי' always introduces a challenge from a source with authority, usually a ברייתא or משנה. After the previous steps ended by supporting the idea that a בעל קרי is sent outside two camps, we should expect this new source to push back on that conclusion. Wait for the quoted text before deciding what exactly is being challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: "They raised an objection": the formula that introduces a challenge from an authoritative source such as a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: 'מֵיתִיבִי' by itself does not tell you what the problem is. It only tells you a problem is coming, so do not try to work out the objection until the next line quotes the source.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
phrases.notes: A formula that introduces a challenge from a ברייתא or משנה. The quoted source follows on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge after the previous back-and-forth was resolved in Step 18, presumably against the view (supported in Step 14) that a בעל קרי is sent outside two camps.
steps.kashyaTarget: Most likely רבי יוחנן's position that a בעל קרי is sent outside two camps; this will be confirmed once the source is quoted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not yet stated. The challenge will come from the authoritative source that the גמרא quotes in the next line.
